title: Learning When to Denoise: Asynchronous Schedules for Faster Multi-Representation Diffusion Training
claim: Denoising complementary representations on an asynchronous schedule lets coarse semantic structure form first and guide later fine texture refinement.
layout: 2 rows of image strips left, schedule plot right, shared time axis
description: The figure has two parts. On the left, two rows of six square image thumbnails show denoising progress at global times τ = 0.00, 0.31, 0.54, 0.74, 0.90 and 1.00. The top row, outlined in teal and labeled Sem. (DINO), shows a PCA-colored semantic latent. It turns from noise into a clear bird silhouette by the middle columns. The bottom row, outlined in orange and labeled Tex. (image), stays as noisy texture for most columns. A sharp photo of an eagle on a log appears only in the last two columns. On the right, a line plot of t against τ shows a straight teal line, t_sem = τ, and a convex orange curve, t_tex = f(τ), that lies below it. Dashed vertical lines with dots link the plot to the thumbnail columns. The eye goes first to the colorful thumbnails, then to the diverging curves.
caption: Learning the relative denoising schedule between semantic and texture latents. Along a shared global time \(\tau\), the semantic branch follows \(t_{\sem}=\tau\), while the texture branch follows a learned schedule \(t_{\tex}=f^\star(\tau)\le\tau\). Since larger \(t\) denotes a cleaner latent, semantic structure is formed earlier and guides subsequent texture refinement. The dashed lines mark the trajectory states visualized on the left.
abstract: Multi-representation diffusion models can improve visual synthesis by denoising complementary views of an image, but their performance depends critically on the asynchronous schedule that determines when each representation is denoised. We propose to learn this schedule. Our method formulates asynchronous flow matching over multiple representation spaces and uses a schedule-corrected objective that keeps each representation's local noising-time weights fixed as the schedule changes. We instantiate the schedule with a flexible parametric class that is convex and monotone by construction, and learn it using a fast joint probe with less than (1\%) additional training compute. On ImageNet (256\times256), the learned schedule substantially improves both convergence speed and final quality under a matched (675)M-parameter XL backbone. With AutoGuidance, our (200)-epoch model reaches FID (1.05), matching the (800)-epoch SFD-XL baseline with (4\times) less training. Training to (600) epochs achieves \textbf{FID 1.02, below the 1.04 of the 1B-parameter SFD-XXL while using fewer parameters.} In the unguided setting, our (200)-epoch model reaches FID (2.37), already below the best (800)-epoch SFD-XL result ((2.54)) at (4\times) less training, and improves to FID (2.14) at (600) epochs. Code is available at https://github.com/bsq532087/LWD.
